land.text: Hà Tiên, Phú Quốc and the Gulf of Siam coast to Lũng Kỳ (Kep): the Mạc clan's settlements

predecessors.note: Hà Tiên 'had been a part of Cambodia for a long time' and 'until the year 1714' (Mạc Cửu page); Mạc Cửu held an Okna title from the Cambodian king between 1687 and 1695.

land.text: Hà Tiên, Phú Quốc and the Gulf of Siam coast to Lũng Kỳ (Kep): the Mạc clan's settlements

successors.note: Hà Tiên Province formed in 1832; the Siamese held Hà Tiên briefly in January 1834 (nguyen-dynasty ledger).

capitals.name: Hà Tiên
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Hà Tiên'; Mạc Cửu fled to Lũng Kỳ (Kep) in 1715.

rulers.name: Mạc Cửu
rulers.note: Infobox 1707-1735; the text says he died in 1736 (the Mạc Cửu page has 18 July 1735, 16 July 1735 and 1736).

rulers.name: Mạc Thiên Tứ
rulers.note: Table 1736-1771; the Mạc Thiên Tứ page has 18 July 1735.

rulers.name: Mạc Thiên Tứ (restored)
rulers.note: Returned after Taksin's occupation; imprisoned by Taksin in 1780.

rulers.name: Mạc Tử Thiêm
rulers.note: After him the Nguyễn appointed rulers directly.

correction.text: Hà Tiên, Phú Quốc and the Gulf of Siam coast to Lũng Kỳ (Kep): the Mạc clan's settlements

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Hà Tiên row; the Gulf of Siam coast sits inside its 'Cambodia' row 1700-1802, and nguyen-lords takes 17 of its western cells in 1755). The pages give a town, 'seven villages in Phú Quốc, Lũng Kỳ' and, undated, lands ceded by Outey II, and no frontier or area, so one 80 km circle round Hà Tiên is drawn for the whole life. Infobox area: not stated.

region.text: Hà Tiên, Phú Quốc and the Gulf of Siam coast to Lũng Kỳ (Kep): the Mạc clan's settlements

ledger.note: 1707: Mạc Cửu turns Hà Tiên to the Nguyễn. 'Mạc Cửu switched allegiance to the Nguyễn lords of Vietnam in 1707, just after an invasion by Siam'; infobox status 'Vietnamese protectorate (1707-1832)'. The Mạc Cửu page has the tribute mission in 1708 and Hà Tiên 'a part of Cambodia until the year 1714'.

region.text: Hà Tiên, Phú Quốc and the Gulf of Siam coast to Lũng Kỳ (Kep): the Mạc clan's settlements

ledger.note: 1771: Taksin takes Hà Tiên. 'In 1771, Siamese army led by Taksin and Phraya Phiphit landed at' Kampong Som and Kampot, then 'besieged and captured Hà Tiên'; Taksin appointed Tang Lieng governor. The Thonburi dossier dates the fall to November 1771.

region.text: Hà Tiên, Phú Quốc and the Gulf of Siam coast to Lũng Kỳ (Kep): the Mạc clan's settlements

ledger.note: 1773: Mạc Thiên Tứ returns. 'Two years later, with the help of Nguyễn lord' he took Hà Tiên back (his restored reign is 1773-1777 on the Principality page).

region.text: Hà Tiên, Phú Quốc and the Gulf of Siam coast to Lũng Kỳ (Kep): the Mạc clan's settlements

ledger.note: 1832: Hà Tiên is annexed. 'Hà Tiên trấn was disestablished in 1832' and Hà Tiên Province formed in its area; the Nguyễn had appointed the ruler directly since 1809, after a Siamese protectorate 1785-1809.

wars.name: Cambodian-Siamese invasion of Hà Tiên (1715)

zones.text: Hà Tiên, Phú Quốc and the Gulf of Siam coast to Lũng Kỳ (Kep): the Mạc clan's settlements

wars.outcome: Thommo Reachea III of Cambodia, with Siamese support, defeats Mạc Cửu, who flees to Lũng Kỳ (Kep); the page does not say how Hà Tiên was recovered.
wars.note: Mạc Cửu page: 'In 1715, the Cambodian king, Thommo Reachea III ... invaded Hà Tiên with the support of Siam.' Not on the Principality page.

wars.name: Cambodian invasion of Hà Tiên (1739)
wars.outcome: A Cambodian army led by 'Nặc Bồn' invades Hà Tiên and is 'utterly defeated' by Mạc Thiên Tứ; no change of border.

wars.name: Siamese conquest of Hà Tiên (1771)

zones.text: Hà Tiên, Phú Quốc and the Gulf of Siam coast to Lũng Kỳ (Kep): the Mạc clan's settlements

wars.outcome: Taksin captures Hà Tiên in 1771; Mạc Thiên Tứ returns with Nguyễn help in 1773.
wars.note: Thonburi dossier: Siamese withdrew from Cambodia and Hà Tiên in 1773.

certainty.note: A port principality: the pages name towns and villages, never a frontier.

sources.title: Principality of Hà Tiên
sources.note: Identity, status (Cambodian protectorate 1707-1736, Vietnamese 1707-1832, Siamese 1785-1809), 1707, 1739, 1771, 1785, 1809, 1832, rulers table. No area.

sources.title: Mạc Cửu
sources.note: Mạc Cửu: Okna title 1687-95, tribute mission 1708, Hà Tiên Cambodian to 1714, the 1715 invasion, death 1735/36.

notes: State Cliopatria lacks; named by se-01-h (cambodia, nguyen-lords). Three pages opened. Not settled: (1) founding: the Principality page says 'late 17th century' (Mạc Cửu left Leizhou in 1671) with allegiance to the Nguyễn in 1707, the Mạc Cửu page has the tribute in 1708 and a Cambodian Hà Tiên to 1714; 1707 is the infobox year; (2) extent: no page lists the 'seven districts' or the lands ceded by Outey II (undated); an 80 km circle is used throughout, so Rạch Giá, Cà Mau and Long Xuyên, which nguyen-lords takes from Cambodia in 1755, are not counted as Hà Tiên land; (3) the Cambodian-protectorate years 1707-1736, the Siamese protectorate 1785-1809 and the Nguyễn appointment of rulers from 1809 are overlordships whose vassal pairs belong to post-angkor-cambodia, rattanakosin-kingdom and nguyen-dynasty (none exists yet); (4) the 1715 invasion's end is undated; (5) the Mạc Thiên Tứ page names his reign 1735-1771 and 1773-1777, the Principality table 1736-1771; (6) Hà Tiên was held by the Siamese again in January 1834 (nguyen-dynasty ledger), after this state's end.
